title: lefthook.yml invariants
description: What a lefthook.yml may contain. Two rules, both written down as decisions and neither enforceable by a comment: a job is one command with arguments, and the file names no container. Checked with check-jsonschema; see the `lefthook-invariants` job.

templates.description: Declared here, filled per machine in lefthook-local.yml. An empty string is the only value this file may carry — anything else names where a tool comes from, which is a property of the machine and not of the repository.

extends.description: Local configs merged into this one — how a repository that ships a contract consumes its own.

remotes.description: Configs fetched from a git repository and merged into this one — how a consumer takes a contract, pinned by `ref`. The invariants hold for the remote config as well; check it where it is written, not where it is fetched.

ref.$comment: required: an unpinned remote follows the default branch, and the gate then changes under a commit that changed nothing

command.description: One command with arguments. Under Windows lefthook passes the whole string to the shell as one composite argument (evilmartians/lefthook#1167), where quoting collapses and a command substitution arrives already split.

allOf.$comment: no multi-line block — put the logic in a wrapper
no pipe, no chaining, no separator
no container reference — dispatch belongs to the calling layer
